summary: Steel fire tower near Blaney in Kershaw County, listed among seven new steel towers erected in the state's 1937-38 report and marked removed on Eastern US Lookouts; no source describes the site today.

facts.status_note: Eastern US Lookouts marks the tower Removed, with no date given.

events.note: Florence Morning News item dated July 19, 1936, quoted by Eastern US Lookouts: district forester sought an additional tower site near Blaney, which would make five towers for Kershaw County.
The state report for July 1937 to June 1938 lists Blaney in Kershaw County among seven new steel fire towers erected that year. Year given is the one the report period ends in.

evidence.supports: 1936: district forester trying to secure an additional tower site near Blaney, making five towers for Kershaw County
evidence.quote: District Forester Hieger is at present attempting to secure an additional tower site in the vicinity of Blaney, which will make in all five towers for Kershaw county.

evidence.supports: Blaney in Kershaw County was one of seven new steel fire towers erected in the 1937-38 report year
evidence.quote: Seven new steel fire towers were erected, including Blaney in Kershaw County.

evidence.supports: The Civilian Conservation Corps built towers and telephone lines that year at no cost to the state or protective associations
evidence.quote: Additional towers and telephone lines were constructed during the year by the Civilian Conservation Corps at no cost to the State or protective associations.

evidence.supports: Blaney was one of five sites that received tower unit buildings
evidence.quote: Tower unit buildings consisting of a four room dwelling, barn, smoke house, chicken house and latrine were constructed at five tower sites. Blaney being one of these sites.

evidence.supports: Eastern US Lookouts marks the Blaney tower as removed
South Carolina phased out its towers in the early 1990s; only 30 still standing when the article was written
evidence.quote: South Carolina phased out its towers in the early 1990s. Today, only 30 of them remain standing.

sources.title: Looking out for last fire towers

notes_for_editor: The 1936 and 1937-38 facts come only from the Eastern US Lookouts page, which quotes a Florence Morning News item and the state forestry report; neither original was read directly. No staffing, access or visit data found. A search snippet claiming five complete Kershaw tower units in a 1944 newspaper was not verified (the cached newspaper page was a stub) and is not used. A snippet about a Kershaw County Historical Society piece on Blaney becoming Elgin was not read and is not used. TopoQuest also lists Buffalo and Cassatt lookout towers in Kershaw County; these are not linked to Blaney and are not used. The brief coordinates 34.1713, -80.7829 are not verified by any source here.
